routeSelection.basis: The Dutch-taught National and International Politics route is the current broad Politics option for new entrants. The separate English-language International Relations and Organisations route is not used for this example.

comparator.name: Political Science
comparator.sourceNotes: The current Dutch-taught route has 60 EC of first-year coursework, with separate mentoring. The official curriculum chart lists 35 EC of required second-year coursework and five 5 EC restricted courses. The third-year chart shows 30 EC of open electives, a 10 EC seminar and a 20 EC thesis. The programme description confirms a supervised individual thesis. The programme regulations refer to the Study Guide for compulsory sequencing. The current route catalogue and Appendix 1 do not supply the detailed later-year rules. The later-year tables for International Relations and Organisations and the outgoing Dutch routes cover different cohorts or routes.
components: Politics and Policy-Making and Academic Skills 2

Introduction to Statistics and Data Analysis
Politics of the European Union and Academic Skills 4
Students choose five 5 EC courses from the published list.
Students may choose electives, a minor, study abroad or an internship.
Students design and carry out their own political science research with supervision. Entry requirements for this route still need confirmation.

audience.programmeDescription: Leiden’s National and International Politics route studies power, institutions and public policy in the Netherlands, Europe and the wider world. It develops comparative, qualitative and quantitative research skills and ends with a supervised individual thesis.
audience.comparisonExplanation: Leiden’s curriculum chart shows how the 180 EC degree is organised. The detailed later-year course and progression rules are still under review, including entry to the seminar and thesis.
